schematic.title: DIY capacitor-discharge pulse-arc welder (jewelry)

notes.title: Firmware behaviour (modelled in WireLab)
lines: 1. Boot: K1 and K2 released (K2 released = bank dumping through R6); disarmed until S1 reads OFF (from 1 s after boot), then ON.
2. ARM switch S1 read on GPIO3 through R7/R8 (12 V -> 2.11 V): ON above 8 V, OFF below 6 V.
3. Arming (S1 ON, no latch, DUMP not held, no fault): wait until the bank is < 5 V, energize K2, wait 60 ms, close K1 (CHARGE).
4. Open K1 once V + rise rate x (10 ms relay release + sample interval) reaches set point - 3 V; the rate is the positive slope, lightly smoothed (READY).
5. Disarm (S1 OFF, DUMP, any FAULT): K1 off at once, K2 released 20 ms later; DUMPING until < 5 V for 200 ms, then SAFE.
6. A DUMP press latches: disarmed until S1 reads OFF and then ON; nothing arms while DUMP is held.
7. Dump stalled (not halved in 1 s, or > 30 V after 3 s): FAULT DUMP STALLED, "switch ARM off".
8. Hard cutoff above 310 V; 30 s charge timeout; no rise past 30 V within 0.8 s (pen on work / short): FAULT.
9. Faults clear when S1 goes ON -> OFF (once the bank is < 310 V) or on a 1 s BOOT hold; arming again needs S1 OFF -> ON. A short BOOT press cycles 120/180/240/280 V.
READY keeps K1 open; a >= 20 V drop between samples counts as a weld -> HOLD 1.5 s -> recharge.
LCD: state bar, bank volts, stored joules, set point, bar graph, weld count, raw ADC mV and ARM supply volts.

notes.title: Grounding
lines: U1 is non-isolated: PS1 -, the bank -, the pen and the ESP32 GND are ONE node.
K2, R8, R9, R10 and the DUMP button return to that same node.
PS1 must be floating. Never connect U2's USB to a PC while the bank is energized.
DCEN: pen (electrode) on -, work clamp on +.
Weld leads W1/W2 (12 AWG silicone, 600 V) solder straight to cap legs of opposite caps, never through board copper. Keep them short and twisted.

notes.title: Safety flags
lines: - Shock: with DCEN the clamp and the workpiece sit at +300 V against the pen, the ESP32 GND/USB-C shell, the power bank and PS1 -. Never hold the work in a bare hand while the bank is charged; the pen's metal pin vise is on the - node.

- K2 dumps the bank through R6 (1 k x 190 uF, tau 0.19 s: 300 V -> < 5 V in ~0.8 s) whenever it is released: disarm, DUMP, fault, reset, panic or power loss. The 302 k bleeder (tau 57 s) stays as the backup; U1's own output capacitors are on the same node. Measure before touching.
- R6 takes 8.5 J per dump from 300 V, 0.3 A / 90 W for an instant: use a >= 10 W cement or wirewound 1 k rated for >= 330 V, mounted in the case away from plastic.
- S1 is the hardware interlock: with S1 off the charger has no input power whatever the firmware does. S1 must be rated >= 5 A at 12 V DC.
- Never energize K2 while the bank is >= 5 V: K2's contacts are rated 10 A at 30 V DC, so opening a live 300 V dump current could arc. The firmware waits for < 5 V first.
- R9/R10 (10 k) hold K1.IN and K2.IN low through reset and boot: K1 stays open and K2 stays released (dumping) until the firmware runs. Confirm both modules switch reliably from 3.3 V.
- U1 can reach 390 V but C1/C2 are rated 330 V: U1's pot is the only hardware limit. Set it to ~300 V unloaded, then lock it (glue or paint).

- Near the set point the bank rises ~500-700 V/s; at a 10 ms loop the relay cutoff overshoots 5-7 V. Sample fast (>=1 kHz) or keep the set point well under U1's pot setting. The 310 V cutoff is only 10 V above the 300 V ceiling.

- Board clearance: 2.54 mm pitch gives < 3 mm between neighbouring strips and between the + and - rails. A 300 V + rail beside the - rail breaks the 3 mm rule whatever the copper width (see the perfboard check).
- The underside C1+<->C2+ and C1-<->C2- jumpers each carry about half of the weld pulse (simulated peak ~1 kA total). Use 12 AWG or bend the cap legs together; thin jumper wire will fuse.
- Wire insulation on every 300 V jumper (blue, brown, U1 output, K2 COM/NC, R6) must be rated >= 300 V; silicone 600 V wire is the safe pick.

- D1 (Vf ~0.6 V) clamps ADC_IN near 3.9 V, above the C6's 3.6 V absolute maximum. R5 limits the excess current to well under 1 mA so the pin survives, but a Schottky (BAT54/BAT85) clamps tighter, and the clamp current flows into the 3V3 rail.
- PS1 must truly float: check with a meter that PS1 - has no continuity to the plug's earth pin (many bricks tie it through the barrel or a Y-capacitor).
- 12 AWG weld leads are stiff: strain-relieve them so they do not lever the photoflash cap legs or their solder joints.
